blocks.text: Agurker danner meget lidt ethylen, men er meget følsomme over for det. Ethylen fra anden frugt får dem til at blive gule og rådne hurtigere.

sourceRef.locator: Cucumber chapter, Ethylene Production and Sensitivity, p. 303
sourceRef.quote: Cucumber fruit produce little ethylene, about 0.1 to 1.0 µL kg-1 h-1 at 20 °C (68 °F), but they are very sensitive to it. Exposure to 1 to 5 µL L-1 ethylene accelerates yellowing and decay.

blocks.text: Fødevarestyrelsen anbefaler at opbevare agurker i køleskabet ved 5 °C, pakket i en plastikpose.

sourceRef.quote: Grøntsager - bør pakkes i en plasticpose … Agurk … Hold øje med, at temperaturen i køleskabet er 5 °C.

blocks.text: Ved længere opbevaring trives agurker bedst ved 10–12,5 °C og høj luftfugtighed (95 %).

sourceRef.locator: Cucumber chapter, Optimum Storage Conditions, p. 303
sourceRef.quote: Recommended conditions for commercial storage of cucumbers are 10 to 12.5 ºC (50 to 54 °F) at 95% RH (Hardenburg et al. 1986).

blocks.text: Plastfolie mindsker vandtabet – derfor er drivhusagurker ofte pakket ind.

sourceRef.locator: Cucumber chapter, Retail Outlet Display Considerations, p. 303
sourceRef.quote: greenhouse slicers are wrapped in shrink plastic to reduce water loss

blocks.text: Under 10 °C får agurker kuldeskader efter blot 2–3 dage: små fordybninger i skrællen, gule områder og vandede pletter i kødet. Ved 15 °C bliver de hurtigt gule.

sourceRef.locator: Cucumber chapter, Optimum Storage Conditions; Physiological Disorders, pp. 303–304
sourceRef.quote: Storage below 10 °C (50 °F) results in chilling injury in as little as 2 or 3 days, while storage at 15 °C (59 °F) results in rapid yellowing and loss of quality. … Chilling injury is characterized by surface pitting, increased yellowing and disease susceptibility, and development of water-soaked areas of the flesh.

blocks.text: Kuldeskader kan undgås, hvis agurken spises lige efter, den er taget ud af køleskabet.

sourceRef.quote: Development of chilling injury symptoms can be avoided if chilled fruit are used immediately after removal from storage.

blocks.text: Agurker holder sig generelt under 14 dage; derefter falder kvaliteten hurtigt.

sourceRef.locator: Cucumber chapter, Optimum Storage Conditions, p. 303
sourceRef.quote: Storage life is generally less than 14 days, with visual and sensory quality rapidly declining thereafter.

blocks.text: USDA har testede opskrifter på syltede agurker, bl.a. fermenterede dildagurker, hurtige dildagurker og søde cornichoner.

sourceRef.quote: Dill pickles … Quick fresh-pack dill pickles … Sweet gherkin pickles

blocks.text: Vælg faste agurker i den rigtige størrelse: ca. 4 cm (1½ tomme) til cornichoner og ca. 10 cm (4 tommer) til dildagurker. Brug skæve og mere modne agurker til relish og søde agurkeskiver.

sourceRef.quote: Quality: Select firm cucumbers of the appropriate size: about 1-1/2 inches for gherkins and 4 inches for dills. Use odd-shaped and more mature cucumbers for relishes and bread-and-butter style pickles.

blocks.text: Skær altid ca. 1,5 mm (1/16 tomme) af blomsterenden, og smid den ud.

sourceRef.quote: Cut 1/16-inch slice off blossom end and discard.

blocks.text: Agurker henkoges kun som syltede agurker efter en testet opskrift. Fuldt fermenterede dildagurker kan holde 4–6 måneder i køleskabet, hvis hinder og skimmel fjernes jævnligt – at henkoge dem er en bedre måde at gemme dem på.

sourceRef.quote: Fully fermented pickles may be stored in the original container for about 4 to 6 months, provided they are refrigerated and surface scum and molds are removed regularly. Canning fully fermented pickles is a better way to store them.
